reading: Between the two facing rectangles, the background gap is filled with 8, but the band is one cell narrower at each end of their shared span.

new_rows.name: inner_gap
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X).
bh(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), cell(Y, X1, C1), X1 < X, cell(Y, X2, C2), X2 > X.
bv(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), cell(Y1, X, C1), Y1 < Y, cell(Y2, X, C2), Y2 > Y.
inner_gap(Y, X) :- bh(Y, X), Ya = Y - 1, bh(Ya, X), Yb = Y + 1, bh(Yb, X).
inner_gap(Y, X) :- bv(Y, X), Xa = X - 1, bv(Y, Xa), Xb = X + 1, bv(Y, Xb).

why: every bg cell between the two rectangles on a row (or column) whose neighbours across the band are also between-cells becomes 8; the two end rows/columns of the overlap stay bg

reading: Shapes are diamond outlines; every colour-5 diamond grows by one ring about its centre, every colour-2 diamond shrinks by one ring (radius 0 becomes a single cell), other colours stay; parts off the grid are clipped.
why: each 5 or 2 diamond in the output is concentric with its input diamond, radius differs by exactly +1 / -1 (pair 0's clipped bottom 5-diamond lands one column right of this, apparently an anomaly)

reading: Each closed 1-loop gets a 2 ring on the outside cells touching it (8-neighbours) and a 3 ring on the enclosed cells touching it; loops with a gap are left alone.

new_rows.name: outer_halo
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X).
my(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
mx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
outr(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), Y = 0.
outr(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), X = 0.
outr(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), my(M), Y = M.
outr(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), mx(M), X = M.
outr(Y, X2) :- outr(Y, X), off(DY, DX), DY = 0, X2 = X + DX, bgc(Y, X2).
outr(Y2, X) :- outr(Y, X), off(DY, DX), DX = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, bgc(Y2, X).
hole(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), !outr(Y, X).
closed(O) :- obj(O, Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, hole(Y2, X2).
outer_halo(Y, X) :- outr(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, obj(O, Y2, X2), closed(O).

why: outside bg cells 8-adjacent to a loop that encloses bg become 2 (learned colour), enclosed bg cells 8-adjacent to it become 3; open loops untouched (pair 2 has one extra 2 cell at a notch corner, (13,3), that this misses)

reading: The grid is a 4x6 lattice of 3x3 glyphs; every 1-glyph with the same shape as the single 8-glyph turns 8, then every glyph lying between two 8-glyphs on the same lattice row or column turns 7.

slots.lattice: 3x3 glyph cells at period 4 separated by bg rows/cols
slots.match: all glyphs with the exemplar's shape -> 8
slots.between: glyphs strictly between two 8-glyphs on a lattice row or column -> 7 (shape kept)

why: 8-glyphs are exactly those sharing the exemplar's shape; 7-glyphs are exactly the non-8 glyphs flanked by 8-glyphs in their lattice row or column
invariants: glyphs not matched and not between stay 1

reading: Two small blocks sit at opposite ends; each block's colour floods the gap toward the other across the full grid width/height, meeting halfway (a single middle line stays bg when the gap is odd).

slots.sources: the two coloured blocks at opposite ends
slots.gap: the full-span band of lines strictly between the blocks
slots.split: each block fills the floor(gap/2) lines nearest it; middle line of an odd gap stays bg

why: the lines between the blocks are filled completely, the nearer half with each block's colour

reading: The shape is split by one empty row or column; that whole line is drawn in 3 across the grid.

new_rows.name: gapline
new_rows.datalog:
fgr(Y) :- cell(Y, X, C).
fgk(X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
anyr(Y) :- px(Y, X, C).
anyk(X) :- px(Y, X, C).
gr(Y) :- anyr(Y), !fgr(Y), fgr(Y1), Y1 < Y, fgr(Y2), Y2 > Y.
gk(X) :- anyk(X), !fgk(X), fgk(X1), X1 < X, fgk(X2), X2 > X.
gapline(Y, X) :- gr(Y), px(Y, X, C).
gapline(Y, X) :- gk(X), px(Y, X, C).

why: every cell of the all-bg row/column that has foreground on both sides becomes 3; nothing else changes

reading: A dotted rectangle outline is completed into a solid one, and the small dotted pieces lying outside it are erased and redrawn as solid blocks stacked inside the frame.

slots.frame: dotted rectangle on the dot-lattice, completed solid
slots.pieces: small coloured dot clusters outside the frame (erased from their place)
slots.placement: each piece as a solid block inside the frame, packed side by side / stacked, separated by one line

why: output keeps the lattice pattern everywhere except the frame (solidified) and its interior (packed solid blocks); outside pieces vanish
invariants: background lattice pattern outside the frame

reading: A 1 marker at the top drops down its column; if it lands in a sealed cup of 2s, the cup interior is filled with 1; otherwise (outside a cup or the cup leaks) the bottom row becomes all 1. The marker is erased.

slots.drop: the single 1 marker, falling straight down
slots.container: the 2-walled cup whose open top spans the marker's column and whose floor is closed
slots.spill: bottom row filled with 1 when no sealed cup catches it

why: exactly one of: cup interior (bounded by walls and floor) becomes 1, or the last row becomes 1; marker cell becomes bg

reading: Each 9 square of side s gets a 3 border of thickness s/2 around it and a 1 column of the square's width running from below that border to the grid bottom; layering 1 under 3 under 9.

slots.subject: each solid 9 square (side s)
slots.halo: 3 ring of thickness s/2 around the square
slots.shadow: 1 band, same columns as the square, from below the halo down to the last row
slots.order: 1 drawn first, then 3, then 9 on top

why: every 9 square keeps its place; its halo and downward shadow are fully drawn with that precedence
invariants: cells outside every halo and shadow

reading: Every pair of 1 cells on the same row or column is joined by a line of 8 through the background between them.
why: every bg cell with a 1 on both sides in its row or column becomes 8; nothing else changes
